title: Fiber context bridge and SDK instrumentation hooks for request-local tracing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a lightweight, fiber-aware context bridge plus first-class SDK hooks that guarantee request-local trace/span propagation across asynchronous execution models (Node async_hooks/fibers, Go goroutine context, Python asyncio) with minimal overhead and no memory leaks. This ticket covers: (1) a cross-language pattern for extracting/injecting trace context at entry/exit points; (2) SDK hook API (startSpan/endSpan, annotate, setAttributes) with deterministic flush semantics; (3) an optional auto-instrumentation shim for popular HTTP frameworks to reduce integration friction; (4) compatibility adapters for Redwood edge/proxy header normalization and sampling decisions.

Non-goals: full OTEL SDK replacement, deep language-specific tracing SDKs (we will provide adapters and clear guidance).
acceptance_criteria: Node SDK exposes hooks that attach and propagate a trace context across Promises, timers, and worker threads with no trace leakage after response completion
Go SDK uses context.Context bridge for goroutines and continuations; spans started in handlers appear as children in the global trace
Automatic instrumentation shim for express/fastify (Node) and net/http (Go) that can be opt-in via a single flag
End-to-end traces for a sampled request appear in Redwood Console with correct parent/child relationships and span timings
Benchmark: added p50 latency overhead < 5% and p99 < 10% under representative workload (see benchmark links)
No reproducible memory growth in a 4-hour soak test with 1000 rps per instance
Documentation: integration guide and migration notes published in Confluence and linked in SDK README
updates: 2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Ticket created after observability sprint planning. Problem observed: traces drop across async boundary in customer-reported flow (image gen pipeline).

2026-02-27 Marco Varela: Spike completed — prototype using Node async_hooks and a weakmap-based context registry. Found edge case with worker_threads where parent context not propagated automatically.

2026-03-02 Design review: decided on two-layer approach: a minimal language bridge + higher-level SDK hooks to keep runtime overhead low and allow future extensions (kv-cache tracing, batching annotations).

2026-03-05 Engineering note: discovered race in Node prototype when using nextTick + setImmediate; fixed by deferring context cleanup until end-of-request sentinel is observed. Added sentinel API to SDK hooks.
2026-03-07 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-sdk-node/pull/412 — initial hook API and express shim. Requesting review from @sophie and @liam.
2026-03-09 QA: smoke traces visible in staging console for express and net/http workloads. p50 overhead ~3.2%, p99 ~8.9% on benchmark cluster. Next: extend to worker_threads and add python spike.

2026-03-10 Marco Varela: Locked scope for this ticket to Node + Go adapters and SDK hook surface. Python and Ruby follow-ups to be separate tickets. Created follow-up: ENG-23112 (python-asyncio-context-bridge).
notes: Trade-offs: opting for an opt-in shim reduces surprise for customers but increases onboarding steps; we mitigate with simple CLI flags and templates.
Memory management: using weakrefs/weakmaps in Node and finalizers where available to avoid retaining request-scoped state.
Sampling: sampling decision should be made at ingress (edge/proxy) and propagated via normalized header; SDK will honor header but also expose local sampling override API for tests.
Operational: add a slow-span alert in Console for spans with >500ms duration that correlate with context propagation failures.
